{{Hatnote|This page documents a constructed card pool. Official tournament documents remain authoritative. For the expansion icon, see [[Episode I]].}}
'''Episode I Closed Environment''' is a constructed format in which both decks use only cards with the [[Episode I]] icon. [[Decipher]] introduced it with the [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] expansion in August 2001 as a "stand-alone Episode I only environment designed especially for exciting constructed play".<ref name="crs">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/coruscantrules.pdf coruscantrules.pdf], Decipher, rule card 3B "Episode I Environment" (August 2001). Transcription: [[Coruscant Rulesheet]].</ref> Players also called it '''Type II''' or '''EP1'''.<ref name="dt18697">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18697 Dredlox's Type II HardCore Senators], Neal Razi, DeckTech (31 August 2001): "a type II(Ep 1) dedicated Senate Deck". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017024622/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18697/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="dt19526">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/19526 Dueling Deaths Type 2], Rypcord Kline, DeckTech (28 October 2001): "A Dark Side Ep1 {ie. Type 2} deck". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017002219/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/19526/ Internet Archive].</ref>

== Card pool ==
After Decipher's January 2002 errata, 434 cards in four expansions carry the Episode I icon:<ref name="cardjson">Count of cards with the Episode I icon in [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json swccg-card-json] (Light.json and Dark.json, sets 11–14), Players Committee card database, checked 17 October 2026. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020214323/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

{| class="wikitable"
! Expansion !! Cards with the icon
|-
| [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] || 69
|-
| [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]] || 175
|-
| [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty|Reflections III]] || 61 (62 as printed; [[Desperate Times]] lost the icon)
|-
| [[Theed Palace]] || 129 (the whole set)
|}

Both Reflections III [[Starting Effect]]s carry the icon. Under a Starting Effect, only [[Defensive Shield]]s with the icon may be placed.<ref name="r3rs">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/r3rules.pdf r3rules.pdf], Decipher, "Episode I Only Environment Rule" (October 2001). Transcription: [[Reflections III Rulesheet]].</ref> In January 2002 Decipher struck the icon from [[Desperate Times]], so it is not legal in this format.<ref name="gls">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf ''Star Wars'' CCG Glossary Supplement] (updated 29 January 2002), Decipher, "Desperate Times". Transcription: [[Decipher Glossary Supplement]].</ref>

The Players Committee ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) also allows Virtual cards with the icon, Legacy or Standard depending on the event.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee, "Episode I Closed Environment". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Undercover spies ==
In this format only, an opponent's [[Undercover]] spy does not stop a Force drain from being initiated; the spy cancels the drain once it starts.<ref name="afg" /> For example, with [[Keder The Black]] undercover at [[Tatooine: Watto's Junkyard]] and [[Credits Will Do Fine]] on table, the Light Side player may still initiate a drain there. The Dark Side player places a card on Credits Will Do Fine, then the drain is canceled.<ref name="afg" /> Players used this rule by September 2001.<ref name="dt18746">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18746 Alright who did it this time], Bill Kafer, DeckTech (2 September 2001): "In Ep.1, the undercover spy rules were modified." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261017024334/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/18746/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Organized play ==
Decipher offered exclusive foil cards as prizes and asked players to have their local Tournament Director run Episode I only environment tournaments.<ref name="r3rs" /> Its 2002 tournament resources page carried format notes for the "Episode I closed environment".<ref name="ressw">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020808154840/http://tournaments.decipher.com/resources-sw.asp Star Wars tournament resources], Decipher (Wayback, 8 August 2002)</ref> [[DecipherCon 2002]] ran an "Episode I ONLY constructed" event on 31 October 2002.<ref name="swsched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021023190505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventschedule-otherccg.html Event schedule: Star Wars, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights], Decipher (Wayback 23 October 2002)</ref>
